3. Agrani Bank Ltd, the respondent No.2 before us, filed Title suit No.105 of 1992 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, against the predecessor the instant writ petitioners for recovery of Tk. 75,38,220/-on account of loan taken from the said Bank. The said Bank, having obtained decree against the writ petitioners, on 07.02.1995, moved to execute the decree by filing the said execution case. Attempt to auction sell property mortgaged by the said predecessor of the petitioners having ended in failure, the executing Court issued certificate per section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 in respect to the said mortgaged property in favour of the decree holder bank, and it is that certificate issuing Order dated 12.04.2006 and the Order dated 29.6.2006, by which the said Artha Rin Adalat Execution case was disposed of per section 33(9)of the Ain that are the subject matters of challenge under the instant writ petition, which was filed more than two years after the passage of the impugned Orders. 

 4. The writ petitioners countered that since the impugned decree was passed in a title suit, the Artha Rin Adalat, constituted under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003, had no jurisdiction to entertain the execution case in question. They also asserted that the instant writ petitioners, the progenies of the debtor were not substituted as his heirs on his death, in the execution proceeding, the same is barren of lawful authority. 

 7. As we took up the leave petition, Mr. S.N. Goswami, the learned Advocate for the leave petitioners argued that as section 33(4) or similar provision as in that section of 2003 Ain was not present in the Ain of 1990, that section cannot be now invoked as the execution case was filed before the Ain of 2003 came into force. He went on to submit that since the subject decree was passed by a civil court in a title suit the same was not executable by an Artha Rin Adalat.
